notes: The page continues a letter and carries the author’s 27 at the top. The archive pencil 172 appears at the lower left. No date or title is written on this page.
The opening continuation says that pursuing this resistance à fleur de peau leads to generalizing and deepening the notion of type d’homotopie and developing a homotopical yoga.

The next paragraph moves to sheaves on the étale topos of a scheme X, names locally constant sheaves as the simplest constructible ones subject to a finiteness qualification, and describes constructibility using a finite partition into locally closed constructible strata.

The text then says that the constructible category gives all sheaves after passing to ind-objects and appears itself as an inductive limit of categories associated with partitions. The sentence continues beyond this sheet.

The page’s explicit qualifications are “pour simplifier”, “modulo une condition de finitude supplémentaire assez anodine”, “Supposant X cohérent”, and “(plus une condition de finitude…)”. The ellipsis is preserved; no precise finiteness hypothesis is supplied by the reader.
No proof was attempted. The union and indices were read visually, not treated as a mathematical verification. check_events is therefore empty.
The grammatical mismatch la restriction ... soit loc constant is retained. Mathematics and grammar were not used to supply a final e.
The g of yoga has a descending return extending under nearby letters; this is not read as an independent author underline. The sole clear word underline is beneath constructibles.

Two isolated compact points are distinguished from inferred punctuation: the point between X and (qui on L20, and the additional point near the union index on L15. Neither is assigned a mathematical role or sentence-boundary function.

Parlons is materially indented, supporting the paragraph break. Voici begins at the usual left edge with ordinary line spacing and remains in the first paragraph. No further paragraph breaks are imposed.
No diagrams, independent separator strokes, or margin prose are present. The four guide strokes belong to their four additions and are encoded through their attachment destinations.

All 24 main baselines, four addition lines, top folio number, archive number, quotation marks, underline, two cancellations, inline symbols, and punctuation were inspected against both witnesses. No other reader returns or other-page images/texts were opened.
